newsitem.title: POLAND: Polifarb-W neutral on Cieszyn's merger conditions.
newsitem.headline: Polifarb-W neutral on Cieszyn's merger conditions.

text.p: The board of the Polish paint-maker Polifarb-Wroclaw will recommend to shareholders they accept the new conditions of a merger with Polifarb-Cieszyn which give Cieszyn a majority stake, a Wroclaw official said.
"Our position on the change in the conditions of the merger is neutral and this is what we will recommend to our shareholders," Wroclaw's deputy president Wojciech Solarski told Reuters.
"We, as managers, are interested in the merger and (the change in conditions) is not a major problem for us," he said.
Today Polifarb Wroclaw's PWROa.WA shareholders meet to vote whether to proceed with the merger.

On Monday Polifarb-Cieszyn's shareholders voted to increase a bonus issue of the company to 6.375 million shares from the originally planned 2.98 million shares, with the change giving Cieszyn shareholders a 53.5 percent holding in the new firm after a one-for-one share exchange.

Originally, both companies were to hold 50 percent each in the merged firm, Polifarb Cieszyn-Wroclaw SA, which would command 26 percent of the Polish paint market and account for 40 percent of domestic paint production.
Wroclaw board member Wladyslaw Burczak, present at the Cieszyn shareholders meeting on Monday, told Reuters then:
"It is extremely hard to expect a situation where Polifarb Wroclaw shareholders will agree to a change in an earlier accepted merger plan," Burczak said.
